key_insight: A Transformer-based model that learns serial musculoskeletal changes over time predicted fractures better than baseline-only FRAX in postmenopausal women.
clinical_relevance: Repeated measures of BMD, grip strength, height, and weight may add useful fracture-risk information beyond a one-time clinical assessment.
method: Trained a Hybrid Trajectory-Based (HyTrax) Transformer on longitudinal hip/spine BMD, grip strength, height, and weight.
Added subject-specific slope features from linear mixed-effects models to capture individual trajectories.
Combined HyTrax embeddings with FRAX or baseline clinical factors for ensemble risk prediction.
evidence_signal: In 27,512 WHI participants, HyTrax + FRAX (BMD) reached time-dependent AUC 0.85 for major osteoporotic fracture, and the model was externally evaluated in 1,193 FHS participants with AUC 0.74 for the longitudinal-plus-baseline ensemble.
watch_item: This is a specialized model that needs repeated measurements and external validation across broader, more diverse populations before routine use.
paper_title: HyTrax: Deep Sequential Modeling of Serial Musculoskeletal Measurements for Fracture Prediction in the Women's Health Initiative with External Evaluation in the Framingham Heart Study
